description: Turn a technical drawing — orthographic views, the kind `generate_technical_drawing` produces — into a textured 3D mesh, downloadable as GLB (and FBX, OBJ, USDZ, STL). A drawing is line art and nothing reconstructs 3D from line art, so the server first renders the object the views describe and reconstructs that render; both happen in one call and are charged once. Chaining `render_product` into `photo_to_3d` yourself does the same work and pays for the render on top — 85 credits instead of 80, because here the render is a step of the reconstruction rather than a second purchase. The model follows the proportions of the drawing, not its dimensions — for a mesh that honours the numbers, the drawing has to be modelled in CAD. Typically one to three minutes; the call blocks until the mesh is ready. Costs 80 credits and requires the Studio plan. The GLB is downloaded to disk and its path returned.

detail.description: Mesh density: draft (12k triangles), standard (40k, default) or high (80k).

image.description: The technical drawing (JPG, PNG or WebP): a local file path, an http(s) URL, or a data:image/…;base64,… URL.

output_path.description: Where to save the .glb. Defaults to ./techdrawai-output/model-<timestamp>.glb.

product_name.description: What the drawing depicts, e.g. "wall bracket". Grounds the render, which is what the mesh follows.

style.description: The render the mesh is built from. photoreal (default) keeps materials and colour; clay is matte grey and reconstructs the cleanest geometry, because a specular surface gives the depth estimate nothing to lock onto.

textured.description: Generate colour textures. Defaults to true.

name: drawing_to_3d
title: Reconstruct a 3D model from a technical drawing
